mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (as measured by the series) compresses discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring any specific trigger condition.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.0% in a 3-month window, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce corporate profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a negative S&P 500 return over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue growth expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply-driven expansion (indicated by rising industrial production), manufacturing output growth accelerates corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO growth exceeds 0.5% monthly, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising housing starts series (HOUST) indicates strengthening consumer confidence and residential investment, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as markets react quickly to new construction activity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST rises, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in employment (PAYEMS) and decreases in unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a labor market tightening that accelerates wage growth and corporate costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During a post-shock recovery phase (indicated by rising consumer price inflation), central banks maintain accommodative policies that support equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances during periods when CPIAUCSL rises above 2.0% annually, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
